LESSON: FICTION AND NON - FICTION 2.3.2 NON -FICTION: PERSONAL JOURNAL

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.3: Fiction and Non - Fiction 2.3.2 Non -Fiction: Personal Journal
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Fiction and Non - Fiction 2.3.2 Non -Fiction: Personal Journal, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to keep journals?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. brainstorm the meaning of life- writing and present their findings in class. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication and or be given more considerable time.

2. work jointly to conduct an online search on the characteristics of a personal journal. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, use adapted digital devices, assistive technology or be assisted.

3. discuss the structure of a personal journal and present their findings on a mind map,

4. read a sample personal journal and discuss the content. Learners with speech

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. brainstorm the meaning of life- writing and present their findings in class. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication and or be given more considerable time.
2. work jointly to conduct an online search on the characteristics of a personal journal. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, use adapted digital devices, assistive technology or be assisted.
3. discuss the structure of a personal journal and present their findings on a mind map,
4. read a sample personal journal and discuss the content. Learners with speech

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Fiction and Non - Fiction 2.3.2 Non -Fiction: Personal Journal together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy: This is advanced as the learner uses technology and applies digital skills when conducting an online

search on characteristics of personal journals.

● Critical thinking and Problem solving: This is nurtured as the learner analyses concepts by logical reasoning when

discussing the structure of a personal journal and presenting their findings on a mind map.

Values:
Unity: This is promoted as the learner cooperates with peers to brainstorm on the meaning of life- writing and presents their

findings in class.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Self-awareness: This is addressed as the learner expresses their thoughts, ideas and experiences when writing a personal

journal.
